chapter: Los Angeles nightlife: Sheffield, Hamp and the Cotton Club
title: Hamp and Charlie Wilson jailed over policemen's wives
summary: Joe tells how Hamp and drummer Charlie Wilson were beaten and jailed after fooling around with cops' wives.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah. They had another good drummer around here (him and Hamp was buddies) named Charlie Wilson. Charlie Wilson was originally come from Chicago, I believe. And just before I had my heart attack in Denver (he lives in Denver now), him and I had had breakfast.
This is just recently, you mean.

But they had a little incident. Hamp was quite a playboy, and so was old Charlie Wilson. So they started to fool around with a couple of policemen's wives. And the policemen arrested them and beat 'em up and threw 'em in jail. But nobody knew about it. But two weeks later, everybody said, "Where's Hamp and Wilson?" So

finally, one guy...some musicians came over to where Mutt and I was playing, and said, "Did you guys know old Charlie Wilson and Hamp was in jail, and them cops beat 'em up?" Some guy said, "I told them not to fool with them women, cops' wives." Everybody used to kid Hamp and Wilson when they got out, "You're gonna leave them policemen's wives alone now."
